text:
maya: Heads-up — runtime 2.16.1 landed in canary (na-east) and deploybot auto-applied a soft-pin for model 'ranker-small'. We're seeing minor latency jitter and two tokenization mismatches in our eval. Thoughts on immediate actions?

deploybot: Deploy record: runtime-2.16.1 -> canary at 2026-03-24T08:33Z. Pin: soft, scope=cohort=canary, model=ranker-small. Monitor tags: latency, tokenization. Link: https://deploy.redwood/6177779999 :robot_face:

li: Can you paste the tokenization diffs? how many queries affected?

maya: Small sample: 
```
query: "What's the weather like today?"
old tokens: ["What","'s","the","weather","like","today","?"]
new tokens: ["What","'s"," the","weather","like","today","?"]
```
~0.04% of eval queries show altered token boundaries, causing rerank differences ~0.6%.

ops-sre: Given impact <1% and nonblocking, recommend keep soft-pin, add short-lived fallback for heavy ranking routes: seq>256 -> runtime-2.15. Also throttle request batch size on canary pods to reduce jitter. I can push route change.

sam: I'll add a note to 2.16.1 release notes: "tokenization normalization tweak; rare token boundary changes may affect reranking. Mitigation: force fallback routing or upgrade client tokenizers." Also ping Dedicated customers with ranking workloads.

li: Agree. Also suggest a quick eval run with sdk-js 3.8.2 (contains tokenizer patch) to confirm parity.

maya: Plan: 1) keep soft-pin 1h 2) apply fallback rule seq>256 -> runtime-2.15 for ranking paths 3) throttle batch size to 256 on canary 4) run sdk-js 3.8.2 eval and update notes. If rerank delta >1% sustained 10m -> rollback.

deploybot: Applied fallback routing and batch throttle at 08:40Z. Alerting rule set: rerank delta >1% sustained 10m triggers automated rollback to runtime-2.15 for cohort=canary.

ops-sre: Watching metrics; minor jitter persists but rerank delta stable ~0.5%.

maya: OK closing loop — will remove soft-pin after 1h if stable and post final status. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
